title: Sweet & Sour Turkey Burgers
ingredients: ¼ cup red onion, finely diced (⅛ of whole)
method: Add all turkey patty ingredients (except olive oil) to a large bowl and mix well.
Shape into patties — the base recipe makes 6, but Amy typically gets 9 smaller patties.
Pan-fry in olive oil until cooked through and golden brown on both sides.
notes: Take the extra time to dice the red onion and bird's eye chillies as fine as possible — it helps make the texture smoother. Amy's batch size varies between 6–9 patties; macros are based on 9. Per patty (9/batch): ~11g protein, ~0.5g fibre, ~90 calories.

title: Chicken Sausage & Herby Egg Muffins
ingredients: 12 chicken patties (~87g each, from 1kg chicken mince)
method: Preheat oven to 180°C. Whisk eggs, milk, dill, spring onions, lemon zest, and salt together.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper, pour egg mixture in. Bake 15 mins, then cover with foil for 5 more mins if needed until set.
Cool, then slice the egg sheet into 12 equal squares.
Cook chicken patties separately.
Stack each muffin: English muffin → egg square → chicken patty → cheese slice.
Wrap individually in parchment paper. Refrigerate or freeze.
Reheat from fridge: 10 mins at 180°C. From freezer: thaw first, then same.
notes: Renee recommends making double — freeze half, keep the rest in the fridge. Per muffin: ~446 cal, 38g protein, 39g carbs, 15g fat. The chicken patty recipe is linked separately on Renee's Instagram.

title: 5-Ingredient Maple Sage Chicken Sausage Patties
method: Mix the spices (sage, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper) together.
Add spice mix and maple syrup to the chicken mince. Combine well.
Divide into desired patty size — larger for breakfast sausage, smaller for sliders.
Cook in a hot pan for a few minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
notes: Renee created this for the many people who can't or don't eat eggs but still want a prep-ahead breakfast protein. The psyllium husk is optional but adds fibre. The chicken patties can be used in the Herby Egg Muffins recipe (freeze extras). Macros are per patty for an 8-patty batch.

title: Jammy Eggs in Chilli Oil
method: Boil eggs for ~6.5 minutes for jammy yolks.
Transfer to cold water bath for 5 minutes, then peel.
Add peeled eggs to a container, drizzle with tamari, sesame oil, and chilli oil.
Top with chopped spring onions or parsley.
Serve warm over rice. Keeps for days in the fridge.
notes: Dead simple, high-protein snack. Also good on toast with avocado and rocket. For 2 eggs + 1 cup rice: ~20g protein, ~400 kcal.

title: Protein Pancakes
method: Mash banana. Whisk in eggs.
Add all remaining ingredients.
Cook over medium heat with some butter.
Serve with Chobani low-fat yoghurt and berries.
notes: Reneelynch's note: 'These are dense. Maybe split servings into 2, or if you've lifted heavy weights this will hit the spot.' 47g protein for the full batch. Sub Chief Whey for True Protein — similar macros.

title: Sardine & Yoghurt Dip
method: Drain sardines. Mash with a fork in a bowl.
Add Greek yoghurt, lemon juice, capers, red onion, and spring onion.
Mix well. Serve as a spread on toast or dip with cucumber slices.
notes: Stock Merchant sardines recommended (code BOOBTOFOOD). One tin = ~23g protein. With yoghurt, the full batch hits ~30g protein. Great high-protein snack.

title: 4-Ingredient Chocolate Mousse
ingredients: 1 Tbsp gelatin mixed with ½ cup boiling water
method: Mix gelatin with boiling water and stir well to dissolve.
Add all ingredients to a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth.
Pour into small glass jars. Pop in fridge until set.
notes: Protein-rich dessert — no whey needed. 24g protein per batch (~8g per serve). Add vanilla, orange oil, or peppermint for variety. Adjust sweetness to taste.

title: Sausage Rolls
ingredients: Pinch of sea salt and black pepper
Sesame or poppy seeds, for garnish
method: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line two trays with baking paper.
Mix pork, lamb, garlic, zucchini, carrot, coriander, salt, pepper, and half the whisked egg.
Slice each pastry sheet into thirds. Divide mixture into 9 logs, place on pastry strips.
Fold pastry over filling, overlapping slightly. Press to seal, seam side down. Slice each log into 6 pieces.
Brush tops with remaining egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and flaky salt.
Bake 15–20 min, reduce to 180°C fan-forced, bake extra 10–15 min until golden.
Cool on wire rack to keep base crisp.
notes: Makes 18. Freeze well — serve warm or cold. Great lunchbox protein for kids. ~8g protein per roll, 2 rolls = 16g. Serve with homemade tomato sauce.

title: Sweet Potato & PB Brownies
method: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Mix wet ingredients (excluding peanut butter). Add baking powder, baking soda, and chopped chocolate. Mix in coconut flour.
Pour into lined square baking tray. Drizzle with peanut butter, swirl with a knife.
Bake 30 min, check and cook 5 min longer if needed — should look slightly cracked on top.
notes: No pre-cooking the sweet potato — grated raw into the batter. First shared by Renee in 2013. Add collagen for extra protein. Skip PB and add raspberries for lunchbox-friendly. ~3.4g P per brownie (batch of 9).

title: Zucchini Fritters
ingredients: 4 Tbsp finely chopped dill or chives
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges
2 Tbsp ghee or olive oil for frying
method: Grate zucchini, toss with salt in a sieve over a bowl. Sit 10 min until moisture releases.
Squeeze and wring out ALL liquid by hand, then scrunch in paper towel — the drier the better.
Whisk eggs in a large bowl. Add zucchini, dill, feta, garlic, lemon zest, flour, and baking powder. Stir to combine.
Heat frying pan over medium heat with 2 Tbsp ghee. Scoop ¼ cup portions, cook 2–3 min each side until golden.
Serve with lemon wedges and yoghurt.
notes: Makes 12 fritters. Keep in fridge 3 days or freeze up to 3 months (omit feta for freezing). Delicious with a fried egg on top. Lunchbox friendly.

title: Mum's Chicken Curry
method: Put ghee and oil into lidded frying pan on medium heat. Add cumin seeds and cinnamon sticks — infuse 1 minute.
Add onions, cook 10–12 minutes until golden brown.
Bash ginger, garlic, and chillies with a pinch of salt into a coarse paste. Add to pan, cook gently 2 minutes.
Pour in passata, stir and cook until thick paste. Add tomato purée, ground cumin, turmeric, and ½ tsp salt.
Whisk yoghurt and add slowly to the curry. Cook until bubbling.
Add chicken, lid on, gentle heat ~30 minutes.
Add ground almonds and garam masala, cook another 5 minutes.
Serve with chapatis, naan, or rice. Extra yoghurt at the table.
notes: Ultimate comfort food. Use boneless thighs for convenience. Ground almonds add body without dairy. Serves 4. ~43g protein per serve (curry only).
